resources.title: Choose a name and domain
resources.description: Brief an agent on naming strategy, verify registrar offers, and compare a shortlist against real conflicts.

resources.title: Publish a technical walkthrough on DEV
resources.description: Use Markdown, code examples, and relevant tags to publish a developer walkthrough, and set a canonical URL when cross-posting from your blog.

resources.title: Product Hunt Launch Guide
resources.description: Set a launch goal, choose a date, prepare the product page, and plan how to collect feedback during and after launch.

resources.title: Show HN Guidelines
resources.description: Check whether your project is ready for Show HN, prepare a demo people can try, and invite feedback from the community.

resources.title: Product positioning templates
resources.description: Map competitors, choose a customer segment, and draft a positioning statement to test.

resources.title: Google Search spam policies
resources.description: Check a proposed content or link strategy for search policy violations before you invest in it.

resources.title: AI features and your website
resources.description: Check your eligibility for AI Overviews and AI Mode and learn how their traffic is reported.

resources.title: Claim your business in ChatGPT
resources.description: Check access to Business Hub, claim your business, and keep the details customers see in ChatGPT up to date.

resources.title: Create and share an agent skill
resources.description: Turn a repeated marketing workflow into a skill your agent can load when the task comes up.

resources.title: Product Hunt for AI assistants
resources.description: Connect Product Hunt to an assistant to compare recent launches and draft a listing for your own product.

resources.title: Build a buyer-language testing ground
resources.description: Collect discovery call transcripts, churn interviews, and community complaints in one file, add new objections weekly, and check every new hook, landing page, or offer against that language before it ships.

resources.title: Check your cold email list before you send
resources.description: Read a sample of your list by hand, count the wrong fits, score the rest against a one-line ICP and an exclusion list, and send to the strongest tier first.

resources.title: Rewrite a cold email to be easier to answer
resources.description: Follow a before and after of one outbound email: lead with the reader's problem, ask a small question instead of sharing a video, and give each follow-up its own job.

resources.title: Checklist to get recommended by AI assistants
resources.description: Work through a list of site changes, from letting AI crawlers in to a public pricing page and comparison pages, then ask ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity monthly whether your product shows up.

resources.title: Find prospects from Product Hunt launches
resources.description: Browse recent Product Hunt launches in your category, find the maker through their profile, and send a short congratulations email that offers one idea while the launch is fresh.

resources.title: How 100 founders got their first customers
resources.description: Read notes from 100 founder interviews on where first customers came from, with concrete plays like asking your network for intros, targeted cold DMs, and showing your tool in use inside the communities where buyers already talk.

resources.title: Test several ideas with one cold email send
resources.description: Put up one page per idea, send each prospect a random cold email variant, link positive replies to the matching page, and build the idea that clearly outpulls the rest.

resources.title: Stack distribution channels one at a time
resources.description: Follow how one SaaS added channels by stage, from founder-run outbound to community posts, content, partners, and then paid ads, measuring trials and revenue before adding the next channel and keeping the old ones running.

resources.title: Match your landing page to the ad
resources.description: Check that the angle, promise, and offer on your landing page carry over from the ad people clicked, so visitors keep going instead of starting over.

resources.title: Pick first-customer channels by what you sell
resources.description: Match your first channel to your product type, using patterns from 37 founder stories: direct outreach for B2B tools, money-page SEO for dev tools, short video for cheap consumer apps, and X or Reddit for founder tools.

resources.title: Get customers from small creators' short videos
resources.description: Ten lessons from a solo founder on paying small creators for short videos: pick audience fit over follower count, expect about one yes in 20, pay when the video is live, give each creator a discount code, and track paying customers.

resources.title: Treat launches on X as a repeatable channel
resources.description: A small-team read of an agency's free 40-step X launch checklist: run launches in fixed slots, count small features and customer stories as launches, and give it six tries before judging the channel.
